summary: The starter prompt clearly defines the core goal (a Node.js + Mongoose immutable transaction ledger with multi-document transactions and idempotency via transactionRef). The run-environment fragment (skill_md) supplies critical runtime and cluster details (Node 24, DOCUMENTDB_URI, DB name), so the build can start; several implementation details (API surface, driver/mongoose version, seed/test infra, README and provisioning-as-code) are left to the builder and will be chosen by reasonable defaults unless the author specifies them.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js Mongoose core banking ledger that stores every debit and credit as an immutable document... Use multi-document transactions... Enforce idempotency with a transactionRef field and unique index"
rubric.note: Prompt clearly states business problem and what sample demonstrates.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will implement a single-agent, no-orchestration sample (a standalone Node.js app with local CLI and/or HTTP endpoints).
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't say whether to produce CLI/API/web UI or any agent orchestration.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Node.js 24 with npm and npx is available." (skill_md run environment)
rubric.note: Node.js 24 is provided by the run-environment fragment.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will pick a recent Mongoose compatible with Node 24 (e.g., Mongoose 7.x) and the MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol. The project will pin versions in package.json (exact semver or package-lock).
rubric.note: Prompt names Mongoose but not which release; driver best-practices exist in installed skills but no explicit version.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "A vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol...) is reachable" (skill_md run environment)
rubric.note: Run environment supplies the exact cluster to use and forbids provisioning another cluster.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "connection string is in the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI. Read it from the environment at run time. Never write its value into any file, log, README or test fixture; use a config file or `.env.example` with a placeholder" (skill_md)
rubric.note: Secrets location and handling are specified in the run-environment notes.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "accounts and transactions are defined as Mongoose schemas and models"; immutable transaction documents; account balance snapshot
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Sharding/ shard key is not requested; builder will assume single logical collection (no explicit shard key) unless cluster or scale requirements demand otherwise.
rubric.note: The prompt and reference require schemas for transactions and accounts and immutability for transactions; shard key is not specified.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Provide a small idempotent seed script that creates a few example accounts and initial balances (e.g., 3 accounts, a handful of transactions). The seed script will detect existing data and upsert or skip to be safe to run twice.
rubric.note: The prompt asks to 'verify against the live cluster' in skill_md, but doesn't define sample data content, size, or seeding mechanism.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Enforce idempotency with a transactionRef field and unique index" (prompt)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: At minimum create a unique index on transactions.transactionRef. Also create an index on transactions.accountId and transactions.createdAt (e.g., { accountId:1, createdAt:-1 }) to support recent-activity queries. No additional vector or full-text indexes are required for this ledger sample.
rubric.note: Unique index is required and stated; additional helpful indexes are not specified and will be chosen by the builder.
No embeddings/LLM or vector search requested by the starter prompt.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will expose a small REST API: POST /transactions to post a transaction (body: accountId, amount, type/credit|debit, transactionRef, optional metadata), GET /accounts/:id to read balance and recent transactions; and a CLI script (npm run seed) to load sample data.
rubric.note: Prompt does not specify whether the sample should be a CLI, API, or web UI or the exact routes/inputs/outputs.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Do not provision another cluster unless the run policy says Azure writes are allowed; the cluster above is the one to use." (skill_md run environment)
rubric.note: Run environment mandates using the existing cluster rather than creating resources. The documentdb-azure-deployment skill exists if infra-as-code were requested, but the starter prompt & run notes direct against provisioning.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will add README steps: npm install, copy .env.example -> .env and set DOCUMENTDB_URI, npm run seed, npm start, run integration demo steps; tests: npm test running unit tests that mock the DB or use an in-memory/mock layer.
rubric.note: The prompt asks to verify against live cluster in run-environment, but explicit run/test commands and success criteria are not included.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Acceptance: sample app can post transactions atomically (insert transaction + update account balance in a transaction), duplicate transactionRef attempts are rejected and do not change balance, transactions are not modified after posting. A small demo script exercises these cases against the provided cluster.
rubric.note: Prompt defines the core behavior but not an explicit checklist; builder will infer acceptance criteria from the required behaviors.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Assume this is a sample/demo: no production HA, no multi-region failover, no CMK, and reasonable cost limits; focus on correctness of transactions and idempotency rather than full production security hardening.
rubric.note: No cost or compliance constraints are stated.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Never write its value into any file, log, README or test fixture; use a config file or `.env.example` with a placeholder" (skill_md). Use database named `sample_banking_03`.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Follow standard Node project layout (package.json, src/, test/, README.md); pin dependencies in package-lock.json.
rubric.note: Run-environment guidance specifies environment-variable use and DB name; other repo layout conventions are left to the builder.

contradictions: Prompt says 'Using the DocumentDB skill' but there is no installed skill named exactly 'DocumentDB'. Several documentdb-* skills are installed (e.g., documentdb-driver, documentdb-connection) that collectively cover DocumentDB topics; the wording could mislead a builder expecting a single skill named 'DocumentDB'.
questions_for_author: Should the sample expose an HTTP REST API (recommended) or only a CLI/library surface? The chosen surface will change routes and example usage in the README.
Which Mongoose version should be targeted (or should the builder pick latest compatible with Node.js 24)?
Do you want an idempotent seed script and a minimal test suite that mocks the DB, or is manual verification against the live cluster sufficient?
Should the sample include provisioning-as-code (Bicep/Terraform) for the cluster, or must it strictly avoid any cloud resource creation (use only the provided cluster)?
requirements_at_risk: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository. (Partially covered: skill_md specifies DOCUMENTDB_URI, but prompt doesn't require an explicit .env.example—builder may or may not create one.)
.env.example lists every setting with placeholder values. (Missing: prompt/skill_md advise using .env.example but do not demand listing every setting; builder may omit some settings.)

The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output. (Missing: no embeddings/vector search in starter prompt; skill_md cluster mentions vector-capable, but nothing specifies embedding model or dims.)
The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them. (Missing: not relevant unless AI components are added.)

One database client is created and reused across requests. (At risk: this is best practice and documented in documentdb-driver, but the starter prompt doesn't require it; builder might still do it, but it's not enforced.)
A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data. (Missing: prompt asks verification but does not require an idempotent seed script.)
/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails. (Missing: there is no search/embedding component in the prompt.)
Search results include the similarity score. (Missing: no search component requested.)
Dependencies are pinned in `requirements.txt`. (Not applicable exactly for Node; the equivalent package-lock.json may be created, but the prompt doesn't require pinned dependencies.)
Unit tests run without a live cluster. (Missing: prompt does not require tests or a DB-mocking strategy.)
Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type. (Missing: run-environment forbids provisioning; infra-as-code is not requested.)
The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up. (At risk: prompt doesn't require README contents; builder will likely add one but exact coverage is not specified.)

The sample uses the name 'Azure DocumentDB' throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name. (At risk: prompt says 'DocumentDB' but doesn't require wording conventions; builder may use 'Azure DocumentDB' but could unintentionally use other names.)
